scope: Project-Frankenstein adaptive visual inference, FrankEye consolidation, screenshot specialization and native multimodal vision lineage reconciled against historical Digital Retina learning and current FRANK 0.1 adaptive visual learner requirement

non_overlap_check.semantic_boundary: Drive receipt owns historical Retina dictionary/prototype learning and measurements. This PF receipt owns runtime integration/supersession chronology and cross-source reconciliation.

chronology.finding: Project-Frankenstein introduced an Adaptive Visual Pipeline with Stage 1 YOLO+OCR/scene heuristics (~100 ms) and Stage 2 VLM escalation only when needed, plus region capture and legacy fallback.
chronology.interpretation: This is compute-adaptive inference/routing, not evidence of user-specific online classifier learning. Reusable concept: cheap-first perception followed by uncertainty/need-driven deep escalation.

chronology.finding: FrankEye replaced frank_visual_pipeline.py and frank_adaptive_vision.py with one CPU-only module combining a Digital Retina v8 CNN classifier, DINOv2 INT8 ONNX scene features, fixed visual features, OCR, face detection and optional GoL analysis. The embedded CNN path is explicitly inference-only.
chronology.interpretation: Consolidation reduced service/module complexity and reused frozen perception features, but it removed the earlier explicit VLM escalation engine and did not itself implement personal cyclic learning.

chronology.finding: FrankEye was specialized for screenshots: app/browser-tab detection, improved dark-theme OCR preprocessing, recognition of Frank's own WebUI, and removal of CIFAR-10 classification for screenshots as useless output.
chronology.interpretation: Historical negative result for generic classifier reuse: a classifier can be valid on its training domain yet harmful/noisy for UI perception. Task/domain gating and familiar-UI specialization are required.

chronology.finding: native_vision.py replaced FrankEye entirely with Qwen3.5-4B native multimodal inference through llama-server. The file explicitly removes CNN, DINOv2, ONNX and Tesseract from the path and sends each image plus prompt to the multimodal LLM.
chronology.interpretation: This is a semantic-capability simplification, not adaptive familiarity learning and not evidence of low-cost familiar recognition. It removes the explicit cheap feature path unless another gate exists upstream.

cross_source_reconciliation.drive_retina_learning_strand: Historical Digital Retina implemented real data-driven pattern/dictionary/prototype mechanisms, cached replay and threshold calibration; those are the stronger ancestors of MVC-0/MVC-1 user-adaptive familiarity learning.
cross_source_reconciliation.pf_runtime_strand: Project-Frankenstein separately evolved cheap-first conditional escalation, then consolidated CPU inference, then screenshot-specific heuristics, then native multimodal inference.
cross_source_reconciliation.combined_implication: The current FRANK 0.1 directive is best understood as a deliberate synthesis of two previously separated strengths: cheap/conditional routing from PF plus replayable prototype/familiarity learning from Digital Retina, with modern open-set/provenance/rollback requirements added.

negative_results_constraints.claim: Do not count the February 'adaptive vision' label as evidence that FRANK already had user-specific online visual learning; the evidenced adaptation is inference escalation.
Generic CIFAR-10 classification was empirically useless/noisy for screenshot perception and was removed from the screenshot path.

Replacing the whole visual path with native multimodal LLM inference does not satisfy the current FRANK 0.1 Micro Visual Classifier requirement because it provides neither persistent user-specific familiarity state nor bounded cyclic learner promotion/rollback semantics.
A frozen classifier/backbone prediction must not be treated as sensor truth; historical screenshot-domain mismatch reinforces the current confidence/open-set escalation law.

reusable_candidates.mechanism: cheap Stage-1 visual path with selective deep escalation
domain-specific screenshot/UI recognizers and OCR preprocessing

architecture_delta.preferred_testable_shape: change/region gate -> reusable frozen feature -> user-adaptive MVC familiarity/open-set gate -> familiar fast path OR deeper native multimodal/Retina analysis
architecture_delta.reason: This preserves the strongest historical routing and learning mechanisms without inheriting either generic-classifier domain mismatch or full-VLM-for-every-frame cost by assumption.
architecture_delta.measurement_obligation: Benchmark native multimodal escalation versus feature/prototype fast path on project hardware for latency, CPU/GPU/RAM/energy, known-vs-unknown accuracy, calibration, retention and routing savings.
